dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

binders: A is a real number, universally quantified, subject to A>1.
C is an existentially quantified real constant chosen after A and before any probability space, function, indices, or scale parameters.
In each clause, Ω is an arbitrary type with a measurable-space structure, μ is an arbitrary probability measure on Ω, and X:Ω→ℝ is arbitrary.
In the first clause, i and j range over the five characterization indices but are each required not to be the linear-MGF index.
In the second clause, i and j range over all five characterization indices without exclusion.
Ki is an arbitrary implicit real source scale satisfying Ki>0; Kj is an existentially quantified real destination scale that may depend on all preceding data in that conversion instance.
The internal characterization binders range over λ,t,p∈ℝ as specified by their respective conditions.
hypotheses: Both clauses assume μ is a probability measure and X is measurable.
The first clause assumes i and j are not the linear-MGF index, Ki>0, and the i-characterization holds for (μ,X,A,Ki).
The second clause additionally assumes X is integrable and ∫X dμ=0, then assumes Ki>0 and the i-characterization holds for (μ,X,A,Ki).
conclusions: For every conversion instance in the first clause there exists Kj>0 with Kj≤C·Ki such that the j-characterization holds for (μ,X,A,Kj).
For every conversion instance in the second, centered clause there exists Kj>0 with Kj≤C·Ki such that the j-characterization holds for (μ,X,A,Kj).
The same C, depending only on A, works simultaneously for all spaces, probability measures, measurable functions, ordered pairs of permitted characterizations, and source scales in both clauses.
mathematical_definitions: Tail(A,K): X is measurable, K>0, and μ{|X|≥t}≤A exp(-t²/K²) for every t≥0, with μ evaluated as a real number.
Moment(K): X is measurable, K>0, and for every real p≥1 the real power |X|^p is integrable and ∫|X|^p dμ≤(K√p)^p.
SquareWindow(K): X is measurable, K>0, and for every real λ with |λ|≤1/K, exp(λ²X²) is integrable and ∫exp(λ²X²)dμ≤exp(K²λ²).
SquarePoint(A,K): X is measurable, K>0, exp(X²/K²) is integrable, and ∫exp(X²/K²)dμ≤A.
LinearMGF(K): X is measurable, K>0, integrable, and mean zero, and for every real λ, exp(λX) is integrable and ∫exp(λX)dμ≤exp(K²λ²).
P_i(μ,X,A,K) is Tail(A,K), Moment(K), SquareWindow(K), SquarePoint(A,K), or LinearMGF(K) according as i is the corresponding one of the five constructors.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real A>1 there is a universal comparison factor C≥1, depending only on A, with two simultaneous properties. First, on every probability space and for every measurable real random variable X, any one of the four non-linear-MGF characterizations (tail, real moments, windowed exponential-square, or pointwise exponential-square) at a positive scale Ki implies any other of those four at some positive scale Kj≤C Ki. Second, if X is additionally integrable and has mean zero, then the same assertion holds for every ordered pair among all five characterizations, now also including the linear moment-generating-function condition. The same C works uniformly for every probability space, X, ordered pair of indices, and admissible Ki.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: A is restricted to A>1; C may depend on A but on no later data.

The first clause excludes the linear-MGF characterization both as source and as target. It imposes no outer integrability or centering assumption, although individual selected predicates may contain integrability requirements.
The second clause permits all five characterizations only under the separate outer assumptions that X is integrable and has exactly zero integral.
All conversions are scale comparisons: the destination scale need not equal the source scale and need not be optimal; only positivity and Kj≤C·Ki are asserted.
The universal quantification over ordered pairs supplies both conversion directions only by choosing (i,j) and (j,i) separately; the witnesses Kj may differ between directions and instances.
The implication for a particular Ki is vacuous if its source characterization is false. The proposition does not assert that any characterization holds for a given X.
Measurability of X is repeated: it is an outer assumption in both clauses and also a field of every selected characterization.
The moment condition quantifies over all real p≥1 and uses Real.rpow, not merely integer moments.
The tail quantity is Measure.real, the real conversion of the measure of the event; finiteness is safe here because μ is a probability measure.

The exponential-square and MGF conditions explicitly require integrability of the transformed functions; no convention about an integral of a nonintegrable function is being used to satisfy the bounds.
No symmetry, independence, identical distribution, nondegeneracy, or almost-sure identification of random variables is asserted.
The numerical constants in the displayed predicates are exact as written: for example the linear-MGF upper bound is exp(K²λ²), with no factor 1/2.
